pos.personaBrief: Brazil 2002 used quick transitions and counter-attacks (Wikipedia) behind a back three, with fast forwards, so possession was a means, not an aim.

pro.personaBrief: Wikipedia notes quick transitions and counters; the side was pragmatic and vertical, with wing-backs and Ronaldo running in behind.

est.personaBrief: A drilled back three with wing-backs and fixed roles (shape evidence), though Rivaldo and Ronaldinho moved freely in the front line.

lar.personaBrief: The 3-4-2-1 had no wingers but Cafu and Roberto Carlos as attacking wing-backs (Wikipedia), with the creative stars playing centrally.

blo.personaBrief: Defensive solidity and a back three with disciplined lines; no evidence of a systematic high press in the spell.

mar.personaBrief: No explicit evidence; the back three with a covering centre-back (Roque Junior) suggests zonal cover with a pragmatic mix.

pla.personaBrief: Scolari kept his scheme regardless of opponent, changing only when losing or late (Record), and imposed the back three and his squad choices.

res.personaBrief: A pragmatic, result-first coach who won the World Cup and accepted ugly outcomes in qualifying.

sis.personaBrief: Collective duty came first (Rivaldo covering after the red card, everyone doing their job), and Ronaldo did what was asked of him.

jog.personaBrief: A copeiro team strong in aerial play and duels, but with technical stars; Romario and Djalminha were left out.

bas.personaBrief: Built on experienced players, with 12 based in Brazil and an average age of 26.1, and a few newcomers like Kleberson and Kaka.

lid.personaBrief: Firm authority: he dropped Romario and Djalminha and said nobody would change his mind by force or pressure, though he treated players as a family.
